papers.title: Transcranial photobiomodulation to enhance sleep by elevating adenosine signaling: a translational study.
papers.summary: In mice, transcranial photobiomodulation (tPBM) increased NREM sleep and frontal cortex adenosine, while in vitro near-infrared light boosted cellular ATP without cytotoxicity. A double-blind randomized controlled trial with 40 subjects found that tPBM significantly reduced insomnia severity, sleep disturbances, and sleep latency.

papers.title: EGR3 deletion attenuates developmental and epileptic encephalopathy in Kcna1-null mice.
papers.summary: Using home-cage monitoring and hippocampal proteomics in Kcna1-/- mice, this study characterized a pervasive behavioral syndrome and found upregulation of BDNF and EGR3; heterozygous or homozygous Egr3 deletion prolonged survival, reduced spontaneous seizures and spreading depolarization, and ameliorated BDNF induction, astrogliosis, and proteomic disturbances.

papers.title: Emerging genetics of sleep and circadian disorders.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent genetic advances in sleep and circadian disorders, highlighting newly identified variants in CACNA1D for advanced sleep-wake phase disorder, SIK3 as a familial natural short sleep gene, CADM2 as a hypersomnia driver via variant-to-gene mapping, and BMAL1 ultrarare variants causing a neurodevelopmental syndrome with sleep dysfunction.

papers.title: Juvenile rat's sleep enables schema memory across episodes before expression of memory for individual episodes
papers.summary: Juvenile rats (PD25) were tested on an eight-episode object-place paradigm to examine schema memory formation with or without post-encoding sleep and were compared with a standard single-episode object-place recognition task. Schema memory was expressed only after exposure to spatial regularities and only when sleep followed encoding, while robust single-episode memory was not evident at a 4-hour test, suggesting sleep supports schema abstraction before mature episodic memory expression.

papers.title: At-home limbic-targeted transcranial electrical stimulation during sleep: a feasibility study in healthy adults.
papers.journal: Philosophical transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series B, Biological sciences
papers.summary: In a sham-controlled feasibility study of 17 healthy adults using an at-home limbic-targeted transcranial electrical stimulation device synchronized to N2 onset, active stimulation was associated with longer total sleep time and longer absolute N3 and REM durations, with only REM increasing as a proportion of total sleep time.

papers.title: Cross-Night Modulation of Change Detection ERPs to Foreign Speech Sound Features During N2 Sleep.
papers.summary: Finnish-speaking adults underwent four nights of N2 sleep exposure to tone deviations in vowel /a/ while EEG was recorded. Change detection ERPs P2 and P450 were observed, with P450 amplitude decreasing from night 1 to night 4, but no perceptual learning was found in waking ERPs or behavior.

papers.title: SWAS in SCN1A-related epilepsy: sleep EEG as a window into the evolving phenotype.
papers.journal: European journal of paediatric neurology : EJPN : official journal of the European Paediatric Neurology Society
papers.summary: This editorial discusses sleep EEG as a window into the evolving phenotype of SCN1A-related epilepsy, specifically sleep-wake activity spectrum (SWAS), based on its title and journal context; no abstract was provided.

papers.title: The TyrRS cascade: circadian gating of neuronal DNA repair and its collapse in aging.
papers.summary: Proposes the TyrRS cascade model linking circadian amplitude collapse to neuronal DNA repair failure in aging, integrating PARP1, TRIM28/NuRD, and LIN9/DREAM pathways. Argues that neurodegeneration reflects a scheduling failure (reduced oscillatory amplitude) rather than capacity loss, with implications for chronotherapy and combined repair/clearance restoration.

papers.title: PER2- and state-dependent transcriptional programs gate neural stem cell proliferation with niche-specific circadian autonomy
papers.summary: The study examined circadian dynamics of adult mouse neural stem cells in the subgranular zone and subventricular zone, finding rhythmic BMAL1 and PER2 expression in both niches and self-sustained clock oscillations only in SGZ-derived cultures. Comparative WT and Per2 knockout analyses identified state-specific, clock-dependent transcriptional programs involving ASCL1 and CCND1, with daytime accumulation preceding a nighttime S-phase peak that was abolished in Per2 knockout mice.

papers.title: Effects of different slow paced breathing regimes on cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) oscillations
papers.summary: In 35 healthy adults, fast neuroimaging was used to test four slow paced breathing and paced sighing regimes for effects on cerebrospinal fluid oscillations. All conditions increased CSF oscillatory power and BOLD global signal amplitude relative to rest, but infraslow sighing at 0.02–0.03 Hz produced significantly higher CSF-BOLD coupling than all other conditions, linking respiration-driven infraslow dynamics to neurovascular-CSF coupling during wakefulness.

papers.title: The Glymphatic System in Neurological Diseases: Mechanisms, Imaging Surrogates, and Translational Uncertainties.
papers.summary: Narrative review synthesizing mechanistic, imaging, and clinical evidence on the glymphatic system in neurological disease, distinguishing direct tracer observations from indirect imaging surrogates. Identifies major uncertainties and notes that no noninvasive biomarker has been validated as a direct measure of human glymphatic flow, and no intervention has improved outcomes via a validated glymphatic mechanism.

papers.title: Circadian Biomarkers Before and After the Transition to Spring Daylight Saving Time.
papers.summary: Healthy individuals were assessed before and after the spring DST transition using light sensors, actigraphy, DLMO, and predicted CBT min. The transition had modest, statistically insignificant effects on weekly averages of time in bed, sleepiness, and light-activity synchrony, but slightly delayed CBT min and slightly advanced DLMO and mid-sleep.

papers.title: Periodic oscillatory slowing and aperiodic broadband shifts in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder are associated with phenoconversion.
papers.summary: In 134 iRBD patients and 51 controls, periodic and aperiodic EEG components were separated using FOOOF. After aperiodic removal, iRBD showed higher periodic 4-8 Hz power, and converters exhibited more oscillatory slowing and higher occipital aperiodic offset; higher posterior periodic 4-8 Hz power and offset were associated with phenoconversion risk.

papers.title: Daily associations between outdoor air pollution and sleep quality
papers.summary: Using 7-day observational data from the Budapest Sleep, Traits and Experiences Study, the authors tested daily associations of outdoor PM2.5, NO2, and O3 with self-reported and EEG-measured sleep. Elevated O3 on day 1 was associated with lower sleep efficiency and poorer perceived sleep quality on night 2, while no robust day-to-night associations emerged for any pollutant.

papers.title: Montage-guided fusion network for long-term scalp electroencephalography seizure detection.
papers.summary: Proposes MGF-Net, a montage-guided fusion network that models 18 bipolar EEG derivations as nodes in a relation-labeled graph with a graph Transformer for seizure detection. On the CHB-MIT dataset, it achieved event-level sensitivity of 100% with a false detection rate of 0.82/h and latency of 2.03 s.

papers.title: Heart rate variability and sleep monitoring using single-channel PPG signal analysis: techniques and applications.
papers.summary: Develops a single-channel PPG-based method (SCH-HSA) using variational mode decomposition, Hilbert transform, sample entropy, particle swarm optimization, and Bi-LSTM for HRV estimation and sleep staging. Achieves 94.6% HRV estimation accuracy and 95.2% sleep-stage classification accuracy, outperforming several existing methods.

papers.title: Cell-Autonomous and Systemic Circadian Regulation of Gene Expression in Adipocytes.
papers.summary: Deeply sequenced in vitro-differentiated adipocytes over a 2.5-day circadian time-course and compared with in vivo adipose tissue datasets, finding 21% of the protein-coding transcriptome rhythmic. Motif enrichment revealed temporally distinct early E-box activator and late nuclear receptor-associated regulatory programs in adipocytes.

papers.title: Factors associated with sleep state misperception in patients with obstructive sleep apnea: a cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional study of 700 OSA patients classified into negative, normal, and positive sleep state misperception groups based on Sleep Perception Index. Higher AHI was independently associated with both misperception directions, with positive misperception linked to objective sleep architecture disruptions and negative misperception to psychological and cognitive factors.

papers.title: A future 'rodentopia'? Imagining a good life for rats and mice used in research (and the humans who work with them).
papers.summary: Invited perspective imagining a future (2066) 'rodentopia' where societal attitudes toward rats and mice are transformed, leading to radically improved laboratory conditions, voluntary participation, and 'research clinics' using companion rodents. Argues that high welfare enhances scientific validity, replicability, and translational success.

papers.title: Home video-only recording in epilepsy care: clinical applications, technological platforms, and future directions.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: Reviews home video-only recordings (HVR) in epilepsy care, covering clinical applications, platforms, benefits, limitations, and AI integration. Reports that HVR shows high accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity for distinguishing epileptic seizures from non-epileptic spells, and offers lower cost and greater accessibility than video-EEG.

papers.title: Systemic inflammatory profiles associated with early EEG abnormalities following ischemic stroke: a cohort study.
papers.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: Retrospective cohort of 307 acute ischemic stroke patients examined associations between peripheral inflammatory biomarkers and early EEG abnormalities within 72 h. Elevated neutrophil count was independently associated with epileptiform discharges (OR 1.19) and improved prediction, while slow activity was mainly predicted by stroke severity and hemorrhagic transformation.

papers.title: Temporal Immune Surveillance in Cancer: A Circadian Framework from Mechanisms to Chronotherapeutic Integration.
papers.summary: This review proposes 'temporal immune surveillance' as a circadian-regulated process and describes a multi-tiered regulatory network involving immune cell clocks, clock-controlled gene networks, and systemic neuro-immune and microbiota-immune axes. It outlines a chrono-immunotherapy strategy with three integrated pillars: optimizing timing of existing therapies, pharmacologically reprogramming disrupted circadian clocks, and pre-synchronizing host physiology through lifestyle interventions.

papers.title: Connectivity- and frequency-individualized accelerated intermittent theta burst stimulation in treatment-resistant depression: A randomized controlled trial.
papers.summary: In a randomized, placebo-controlled trial with 51 treatment-resistant depression patients, accelerated intermittent theta burst stimulation individualized by fMRI connectivity, with or without EEG frequency personalization, failed to show significant antidepressant benefits over sham stimulation on the primary MADRS outcome at 1 week post-treatment or on secondary anhedonia measures. Remission and response rates also did not differ between arms, underscoring the need for further trials of personalized aiTBS.

papers.title: Effectiveness of GLP-1 receptor agonists to prevent obstructive sleep apnea in patients with type 2 diabetes: active comparator, new user cohort study.
papers.journal: American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine
papers.summary: In a population-based cohort study using UK CPRD data with 47,315 GLP-1RA and 159,066 DPP-4i initiators with type 2 diabetes and BMI ≥30, GLP-1RA use was not associated with a reduced risk of incident obstructive sleep apnea compared with DPP-4i (HR 1.07, 95% CI 0.93-1.23) over up to 3 years of follow-up. Results were consistent across BMI strata, sex, and sensitivity analyses.

papers.title: Genitourinary syndrome of lactation: An underrecognized postpartum condition affecting women's vulvovaginal, urinary and sexual health.
papers.summary: This narrative perspective review summarizes emerging evidence on genitourinary syndrome of lactation (GSL), a postpartum condition linked to the hypoestrogenic hormonal environment of breastfeeding, and offers a practical framework for recognition, differential diagnosis, screening, and breastfeeding-supportive management. It emphasizes that GSL should not be reduced to vaginal dryness and that management should be stepped and individualized, starting with education, vulvar care, lubricants, moisturizers, pelvic floor physiotherapy, and sexual counselling, with low-dose vaginal estrogen as a reasonable option for persistent moderate-to-severe mucosal symptoms after shared decision-making.

papers.title: Site-specific pain, sleep duration, and depressive symptom trajectories among middle-aged and older Chinese adults with baseline depressive symptoms: A CHARLS-based longitudinal study.
papers.summary: This CHARLS-based longitudinal study of 1047 middle-aged and older Chinese adults with baseline depressive symptoms identified three depressive symptom trajectories (Mild-Stable, Moderate-Increasing, High-Persistent) using group-based trajectory modeling. Site-specific pain at multiple anatomical sites was associated with higher odds of unfavorable trajectories, particularly the High-Persistent trajectory, with only modest exploratory indirect effects through sleep duration (largest indirect-effect proportion ~8.9%).

papers.title: A randomized trial of nefopam for postoperative pain management in obstructive sleep apnea patients undergoing uvulopalatopharyngoplasty.
papers.journal: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
papers.summary: This prospective, exploratory, randomized, triple-blinded trial evaluated whether nefopam reduces morphine consumption and improves postoperative recovery in obstructive sleep apnea patients undergoing uvulopalatopharyngoplasty. Among 51 analyzed patients, nefopam did not significantly reduce 24-hour morphine consumption (median 7 mg vs. 5 mg, P=0.56) or improve pain scores, oral intake time, satisfaction, or quality-of-life scores, leading the authors to not recommend it for this context.

papers.title: Sex Differences in Sleep Duration and Quality: Implications for Hypertension Risk.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence from the past five years on the association between sleep and hypertension, emphasizing sex differences in blood pressure regulation. It reports that sleep duration, quality, insomnia, and obstructive sleep apnea are linked to elevated blood pressure, with emerging evidence that these relationships differ by sex due to hormonal influences and autonomic dysfunction.

papers.title: Accelerated Intermittent Theta-Burst Stimulation for the Treatment of Alcohol Use Disorder: A Randomized Sham-Controlled Study With Six-Month Follow-Up.
papers.summary: This randomized sham-controlled trial tested accelerated intermittent theta-burst stimulation (a-iTBS) vs traditional iTBS vs sham in 61 male inpatients with alcohol use disorder. Although the primary craving outcome did not differ significantly among groups, a-iTBS showed a higher response rate, earlier response onset, and longer abstinence duration at 6-month follow-up than sham.

papers.title: Mindfulness and Tai Chi for Sleep, Fatigue, and Pain in Distressed People After Cancer Treatment: A Partially Randomized Patient-Preference Comparative Effectiveness Trial.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology
papers.summary: This partially randomized patient-preference comparative effectiveness trial evaluated mindfulness-based cancer recovery (MBCR) and Tai Chi/Qigong (TCQ) for sleep, fatigue, and pain in 587 distressed cancer survivors. Compared with waitlist controls, TCQ improved sleep quality (average 1.9 points), and both MBCR and TCQ significantly improved fatigue and pain interference, with no differences between interventions and no effect of preference.

papers.title: Chronotype and Arterial Stiffness: Moderating Effect of Cardiorespiratory Fitness in Middle-Aged and Older Adults.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 1,112 middle-aged and older adults examined whether cardiorespiratory fitness moderates the association between chronotype and arterial stiffness (cardio-ankle vascular index). A significant interaction was found (P=0.007); among those with relatively low cardiorespiratory fitness, definitely morning-type individuals had higher arterial stiffness than moderately morning, neither, and moderately evening types, suggesting the association may be more apparent when fitness is low.

papers.title: Circadian- and light-regulated oscillatory expression of CSA in rice leaves is required for pollen fertility.
papers.summary: The study shows that CSA expression in rice leaves oscillates under circadian and light control, mediated by DOF5 and PIL11 binding to the CSA promoter, and that leaf-specific CSA knockdown reduces pollen viability. These findings link photoperiod sensing to male reproductive development and pollen fertility.

papers.title: Multimodal integration supports neural processing of grammatical negation.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.summary: This EEG study investigated the neural processing of multimodal grammatical negation in Turkish, focusing on how negation gestures and prosodic markers affect the processing of the postverbal negation suffix. Gestures elicited an N100 effect and reduced the N400 amplitude in anticipation of the negation suffix, and prosody strengthened this N400 reduction only when gestures were present, providing neurophysiological evidence that multimodal information supports core grammatical operations.

papers.title: Managing Type 1 Diabetes in Neurodiverse Children and Young People: A Qualitative Exploration of Complexity and Care Challenges.
papers.summary: This qualitative study used semi-structured interviews with 15 neurodiverse children and young people (age 12-18) with Type 1 diabetes and 13 parent caregivers to explore barriers and challenges in diabetes management. Key themes included caregiver adaptation of routines, central role of family support, sleep disturbance from fear of hypoglycemia improved by continuous glucose monitoring, and perceived benefits of diabetes technologies despite sensory challenges.

papers.title: Drawing a Line Between Integrative and Functional Medicine.
papers.summary: This review contrasts Integrative Medicine, an evidence-based academic discipline, with Functional Medicine, a distinct clinical model using nonstandard diagnostic testing and root-cause assessments. The authors argue that Functional Medicine lacks sufficient evidence for its diagnostic and therapeutic validity and may contribute to low-value testing, care cascades, and health inequities.

papers.title: Bidirectional Association Between Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Keratoconus in Young Adults: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study.
papers.summary: In a multicenter retrospective cohort study using propensity-score matching, obstructive sleep apnea with polysomnography evidence was associated with incident keratoconus at 5 and 10 years (HR ~2.0). The reverse association from keratoconus to incident OSA was weaker and delayed, significant only at 10 years, with negative control outcomes null.

papers.title: Measuring motor intent for BCI control-A comparative analysis of signal quality of simultaneously recorded vECoG and scalp EEG.
papers.summary: The study directly compared signal quality of simultaneously recorded intravascular stent-electrode array (vECoG) and scalp EEG in one participant with ALS during attempted motor tasks. vECoG showed stronger motor modulation per channel and was less affected by ocular and muscle artifacts, though it exhibited prominent cardiac activity, suggesting potential for high-quality BCI control.

papers.title: Altered glutamate concentration in major depressive disorder during antidepressant treatment: A glutamate CEST MRI study.
papers.summary: Using glutamate chemical exchange saturation transfer (GluCEST) MRI, this study found lower glutamate-sensitive signals in the prefrontal cortex and hippocampus of unmedicated major depressive disorder patients versus healthy controls. After 8 weeks of SSRI treatment, GluCEST signals increased in these regions, with some correlations between signal changes and symptom improvement.

papers.title: The 6G integrated perception and networking technology enables the low-altitude economy to achieve carbon neutrality: Dynamic sleep strategy for eVTOL wireless charging based on time-energy-carbon coupling.
papers.summary: This study proposes a time-energy-carbon ternary coupling model (TEC-6G) for 6G integrated perception and networking base stations reconfigured as power-information dual-mode supply nodes with sleep states, designed to support wireless charging of eVTOLs for low-altitude economy carbon neutrality. Using real 5G-A base station topology and eVTOL flight paths, a GNN-PSO solution framework achieved 38% base station sleep ratio under ≤2% task delay loss, with opportunistic wireless charging reducing average grid electricity consumption per flight by 27.4% under idealized line-of-sight conditions (11.2% under practical assumptions) and increasing system-level energy utilization from 31.2% to 48.6%.

papers.title: Fahr syndrome in an 18-year-old male with pseudohypoparathyroidism: Clinical-radiological dissociation.
papers.summary: This case report describes an 18-year-old male with pseudohypoparathyroidism presenting with headaches, carpopedal spasms, and depressed mood after medication non-compliance, with extensive bilateral intracranial calcifications on imaging despite largely unremarkable neurological examination. Calcium and calcitriol supplementation resolved spasms and improved headaches and mood at 15-day follow-up, illustrating clinical-radiological dissociation in Fahr syndrome.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
